I pulled together a concise pre-read for the QBR slot (Sept 21 executive session). This thread is the central place for final numbers, slides, and the decision ask we present to execs. High-level context and asks below.

Summary highlights (trailing 30d):
- Committed GPU pool (A100-equivalent): 320 units (reserved + burst).
- Average utilization (last 7d): 62% overall; p95 latency-sensitive workloads show 78% usage during US-evening peaks.
- Current infra spend (GPU only): ~$3.2M / month.
- Forecast demand: baseline +12% q/q; peak scenarios up to +24% with new customers live.
- Estimated token-level cost opportunity: 10–18% savings from combined batching, prefix caching, and 8-bit quantization on compatible models.

Key asks (action owners in parens):
1) Finalize the QBR deck (2 slides): 1) capacity ask + risk matrix; 2) unit-econ levers & ask (Priya). Due: EOD Thu 9/14. (marissa)
2) Run a short sensitivity sheet for 3 scenarios (Conservative +10% capacity / Hybrid: redirect 20% traffic to quantized variants / Aggressive: enable 8-bit + smarter batching). Include cost delta and SLA impact for each. (vivek, karthik)
3) Provide a short one-paragraph exec rationale for any ask to secure additional committed capacity or to pursue purchase credits with vendor partners. (lauren)
4) Ops input: confirm whether Acme AI can shift to our cheaper model off-peak routing if we propose it. (ops@acme.ai)

Attachments: QBR_flagship_draft_v1.pptx (draft slides), batching-impact-model.csv (simulation), quant-profiles-summary.xlsx (model-level quantization compat).

Meeting: I scheduled a dry-run for Mon 9/18 10:00 PT — calendar invite to follow.

Quick notes on tradeoffs:
- Batching gains: best for chat bursts; expected token-cost reduction 6–12% without any model quality regression in our evals; latency SLOs may increase by 20–80ms at p95 if not constrained.
- Prefix caching: high wins for completion-heavy workloads (e.g., customer help flows) — can reduce repeated KV cost by 15–35% depending on reuse.
- Quantization (8-bit): biggest single-line saving (~12–20% on GPU spend) but needs per-model validation for hallucination/QA drift.

Quick sensitivity drop-in from infra economics — attaching a lightweight CSV and past-3-months utilization slice. Topline numbers here so the slide can show clear tradeoffs: 

Scenarios (monthly GPU spend impact / expected p95 latency delta):
- Conservative (add +10% reserved capacity): +$320k / month; p95 latency unchanged, risk buffer for peaks.
- Hybrid (redirect ~20% non-latency traffic to quantized variants + enable batching configs during off-peak): -$210k / month vs baseline (net saving), p95 tail may increase by 30–60ms for affected workloads.
- Aggressive (enable 8-bit quant + aggressive batching + prefix cache TTL tuning): -$640k / month (nominal); risk: per-model quality regression (we estimate 2–5% eval metric delta on generation tasks) and operational validation needed.

Utilization sensitivity: moving 20% of traffic to cheaper variants reduces GPU-equivalent demand by ~8–12%. Batching windows of 50–150ms show best token savings with minimal user-visible latency for async flows.

Attachments: batching-impact-model.csv (detailed sim).

My recommendation: present the Hybrid as the default ask (net saving, low upfront risk) and list Aggressive as a follow-up play that requires model-level QA. If execs push for runway, Conservative is the low-risk fallback.

-Vivek
